clue.text: Parasite showed the way to be mildly amused

parts.note: a tick is a blood-sucking parasite
led means guided or showed the way

explanation.surface: A guide parasite leads people somewhere, which is somewhat entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tickled is being pleased or entertained in a gentle way.

clue.text: A good deal produced by a neat maths student

definitions.text: A good deal produced by a neat maths student

parts.words: A good deal produced by a neat maths student
parts.note: a maths student works out sums, and a neat one would produce orderly ones; the phrase also means a large amount of money

explanation.surface: A tidy pupil turns out tidy homework in arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is an idiom for a considerable quantity of money.

clue.text: Die on finding the fry shop has secretly returned the money

parts.words: on finding the fry shop has secretly returned the money
parts.note: a chip shop hiding returned cash among its fried potatoes would literally have the money inside its fries

explanation.surface: Someone collapses on discovering the chippy has slipped their refund back to them.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'fry shop' is a British chip shop, selling fried potato chips; the cryptic reading pictures cash tucked in among the chips.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash in one's chips is an idiom for dying, from gamblers leaving the table.

clue.text: Beach where topper comes to nothing

parts.note: a lid is what sits on top of a container, a topper
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A seaside spot where a hat ends up worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming place or bathing beach.

clue.text: Sketch which is attractive

definitions.meaning: a sketch is a picture made with pencil
something that pulls in crowds is a crowd-puller

explanation.definitionFit: A drawing is a pencil picture; drawing also means pulling people in, as in a big draw.

clue.text: Inclination the German has to be a Hero-worshipper

parts.note: a lean is a slope or tendency, an inclination
der is the German masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A tendency in a German person to idolise their heroes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth, Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit his beloved Hero, a priestess; the hyphen hides that 'Hero' is her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander was the mythical lover who adored the priestess Hero.

clue.text: Give away so as not to hold things up

definitions.meaning: to reveal a secret casually

definitions.text: so as not to hold things up
definitions.meaning: literally releasing one's grip so objects fall rather than staying held aloft

explanation.definitionFit: To let drop is to mention a secret in passing, or literally to release one's hold so things fall.

clue.text: Classic ship, put to sea sound to get cargo

indicators.note: this reading says the answer has a letter put to it to make the final word, so that letter comes off

parts.note: the word cargo as written
the word sea sounds like the letter C

explanation.surface: An old vessel goes to sea to pick up freight.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: put C (which sounds like 'sea') to the answer to get CARGO, so CARGO without its C is the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the vessel of Jason and the Argonauts in classical myth.

clue.text: Jan Ridd's enemies, unbeaten at evening, so try very hard

parts.note: the Doones are the outlaw clan who oppose John Ridd in the novel Lorna Doone
evening up is making level
the best is unsurpassed, unbeaten

explanation.surface: A fictional clan stays undefeated in the evenings, so one makes great efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is R. D. Blackmore's Exmoor novel; its hero John (Jan) Ridd battles the outlaw Doone family.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one's level best is an idiom for making every possible effort.

clue.text: Puts in a new order for holiday sites

definitions.meaning: sorting things again, arranging afresh
places people go for vacations

explanation.definitionFit: Re-sorts means rearranges; resorts are vacation destinations.

clue.text: Dot again saved us becoming obstructive

indicators.note: the fodder words turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dotting again rescued us yet proved a hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hinders or puts one at a disadvantage is harmful to progress.

clue.text: Slight mistake in speech possibly!

parts.note: a small error, one example being a verbal one made by the tongue

explanation.surface: A minor error, maybe a verbal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a minor blunder, and a slip of the tongue is a spoken one.

clue.text: A book that is dated

parts.note: 'dated' suggests old-fashioned, but here each page carries a calendar date

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A journal has an entry for each calendar day, so its pages bear dates.

clue.text: Better exclude the teetotaller!

indicators.note: to exclude is to leave out, so letters are taken away from the first word

parts.note: TT is the standard abbreviation for teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: Advice to keep the abstainer away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like advice, but it is the word that loses letters; 'teetotaller' is TT in crosswords. The whole clue also reads as a drinker's preference for a pint without abstainers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is an alcoholic drink a teetotaller would refuse, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Small number on hand

definitions.meaning: a single figure from nought to nine
something found on the hand, a finger

explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a numeral from 0 to 9 and also a finger.

clue.text: A calculating snake in the grass?

definitions.meaning: a machine or person that does addition
a serpent found in the grass, literally

explanation.definitionFit: An adder is something that adds figures, and also a venomous viper of British grassland.

clue.text: Low metal loop for tying up boats

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle, a moo
a ring is a circle of metal

explanation.surface: A lowly iron hoop used to secure vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring is the act of fastening a vessel in place with ropes.

clue.text: Gets wet feet while canoeing?

definitions.meaning: wading in shallow water
propelling a canoe with blades

explanation.definitionFit: To paddle is to wade in shallows, and also to row a canoe with a blade.

clue.text: Early look at viper we dissec red

indicators.note: cut up into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A first glance at a snake that we cut open in biology class.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview is an advance showing before the main release.

clue.text: Bird crossing…

definitions.meaning: a large water bird with a pouched bill
a type of pedestrian light-controlled road crossing in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with push-button traffic lights. The ellipsis runs into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a big-billed waterbird, and a pelican crossing is a UK road crossing.

clue.text: … which makes dog happy?

parts.note: a happy dog shakes its rear end; following on from the previous clue's 'Bird', this names a bird

explanation.surface: Continuing on: something that pleases a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries 'Bird' from the clue above: the answer is a small bird whose name describes a happy dog's action.
explanation.definitionFit: The wagtail is a small bird named for its bobbing tail, which a contented dog also wags.

clue.text: Many an ex-school student gets the axe

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
a school leaver is a pupil who has just left school

explanation.surface: Lots of former pupils get sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy chopping blade, a butcher's hatchet.

clue.text: California finishes first day in Rome

parts.note: ends means finishes

explanation.surface: A US state wraps up first, then a date in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The calends was the first day of each month in the Roman calendar.

clue.text: Concerning a player making a pile

parts.note: re means regarding, concerning
an actor plays parts on stage

explanation.surface: About a performer earning a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' looks like a heap of money, but an atomic pile is an early nuclear reactor.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic pile was the early name for a nuclear fission device.

clue.text: Crazy engine

definitions.meaning: mad, slang
short for locomotive

explanation.definitionFit: Loco is slang for mad and short for a railway locomotive.

clue.text: A leg I broke despite being athletic

indicators.note: the letters are broken and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: I fractured a leg but am still sporty.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and quick-moving, as a sporty person is.

clue.text: Jumper liable to cause itching

parts.note: 'jumper' suggests a woolly sweater, but here it is a leaping insect that bites

explanation.surface: A scratchy woollen sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: This parasitic insect leaps great distances and its bites make skin itch.

clue.text: One who pulls strings creates a row

definitions.meaning: someone who ties knots, pulling strings tight
a level or rank, as in seating

explanation.definitionFit: Someone tying string is literally a 'tie-er'; a tier is a layer or row.

clue.text: Commonly against there a being just one short

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Commonly against there a being just one short' gives def 'Commonly against' but no word for AGAIN: 'there a' is likely an OCR misreading of a word meaning again
annotationWithheld.clue: Commonly against there a being just one short

clue.text: Very serious oversight alleged by Prisoners' Welfare Society?

definitions.meaning: a failure of care grave enough to be an offence in law
a group caring for inmates would claim lawbreakers are being overlooked

explanation.definitionFit: A legal term for culpable failure of duty, read also as convicts being ignored.

clue.text: Inspirational opening

parts.note: 'inspirational' suggests uplifting, but here it means for breathing in

explanation.surface: An uplifting start to a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhaled air enters through this opening in the nose.

clue.text: Legislator who disseminates treason

indicators.note: to disseminate is to scatter widely, so the letters are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawmaker spreads betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, a law-making assembly.
